1.explanation: The 'Dropdown' class in 'Dropdown.js' is responsible for rendering the dropdown component, and changes are needed to support rendering elements as selected items. The 'itemToString' function is currently used to convert items into strings for the title attribute, but since it is being hijacked to render elements, this causes the '[object Object]' issue. Adding a new prop or flag to differentiate between 'itemToString' and 'itemToElement' for rendering could resolve the bug.
1.bug_scenario: The dropdown component is used to select icons, but when an icon is selected, the title attribute displays '[object Object]' instead of the icon's name. This is due to hijacking the 'itemToString' function to render elements instead of strings, which worked until a title attribute was added to the button in version 10.43/7.43.

2.explanation: The issue arises from the misuse of 'itemToString' for the title attribute when an element (icon) is rendered using 'itemToElement'. The 'Dropdown' component in 'Dropdown.js' is responsible for handling how items are rendered and displayed. Modifying this component to conditionally use 'itemToElement' for rendering the selected item's title instead of 'itemToString' would resolve the issue. This change will allow the dropdown to correctly display the icon name or a custom element rather than '[object Object]'.
2.bug_scenario: The images show a dropdown interface for selecting icons, where the selected icon dropdown displays '[object Object]' as the title instead of the actual icon name. This occurs when using 'itemToElement' for rendering the selected item visually, but 'itemToString' is incorrectly used for the title attribute, causing the object representation to appear instead of the desired string.
